# Listeners

A listener is a `listener` stanza in a Boundary configuration file. It defines an address and port, or a Unix domain socket path, on which a Boundary controller or worker responds to requests. Each listener stanza configures one address, and each stanza must have exactly one purpose.

You can define more than one `listener` stanza in a configuration file to make Boundary respond on multiple addresses.

## Listener purposes

The `purpose` parameter determines which part of Boundary's functionality starts on that listener. Every listener must have exactly one purpose.

| Purpose | Used by | Description | Default address |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `api` | Controllers | Exposes the controller API. A controller requires at least one `api` listener. | `127.0.0.1:9200` |
| `cluster` | Controllers | Exposes the communication layer between workers and controllers. A controller requires exactly one `cluster` listener. | `127.0.0.1:9201` |
| `proxy` | Workers | Starts the worker proxy that clients connect to. | `127.0.0.1:9202` |
| `ops` | Controllers and workers | Exposes operational endpoints such as `/health` and `/metrics`. The functionality available depends on which Boundary components are running on the instance. | `127.0.0.1:9203` |

The default addresses apply when a TCP listener does not set `address`.

## Listener types

Boundary supports two listener types:

- A [TCP listener](/boundary/docs/monitor/listeners/tcp) listens on a TCP address and port. It is the only type that supports the `proxy` purpose.
- A [Unix listener](/boundary/docs/monitor/listeners/unix) listens on a Unix domain socket path.

## Workflows

1. Define a `listener` stanza for each address on which the controller or worker must respond. To listen on more than one interface, refer to [Configure multiple listeners](/boundary/docs/monitor/listeners/configure-multiple-listeners).
1. Enable TLS on `api` and `ops` listeners. Refer to [Configure TLS](/boundary/docs/monitor/listeners/configure-tls).
1. Optionally define custom HTTP response headers on a TCP `api` listener. Refer to [Configure custom response headers](/boundary/docs/monitor/listeners/configure-custom-response-headers).
